subject: (Possible) Bug with outputting p-values/CIs for lavaan(..., se = boot)

messages.author: edceb8dce9472a62
messages.subject: (Possible) Bug with outputting p-values/CIs for lavaan(..., se = boot)
parts:
Hello, 

First of all, thanks so much to those who create and upkeep lavaan (and this community for the lavaan support). I have been using lavaan for around two years now and have run into the first thing that might be a true bug, so this is my first post here.

I asked for bootstrapped standard errors with 5000 draws to test some indirect effects in a growth model with:

final_fit_boot<- growth(final_mod, data = dat, 
                  estimator = "ML", missing = "fiml", 
                  meanstructure = T,
                  se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 5000,
                  parallel = "multicore")

When I get the output for the p-values and confidence intervals, I get some that do not overlap with 0 and have p > 0.05 (see line 2 of the attached screen shot). 

Some trouble shooting with: [parameterEstimates(final_fit_boot, level = .95, boot.ci.type = "norm", output = "pretty")] gave me confidence intervals which matched the p-values, however.

After playing around with it, my best guess was that the boot.ci.type was set to another method, but even when I explicitly ask for these (by changing the call above to, e.g., boot.ci.type="bca.simple"), I do not get p-values that match. 

Again, the "norm" argument matched, but the others did not. 

Is there a call to change the method used to get the p-value/se that should be set when you change boot.ci.type, or is this a bug?

Thanks,
Chris Loan

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: (Possible) Bug with outputting p-values/CIs for lavaan(..., se = boot)
parts:
Chris,

Bootstrapped CIs (e.g., bca) will virtually always be asymmetric. The p-values you're seeing are based on estimate +/- 1.96*SE, which will always be symmetric. The occasional mismatch is inevitable. And for indirect effects, the asymmetric is preferred because the sampling distribution of the product of coefficients is asymmetric, so can never be accurately reflected by an SE-based computation.

Pat

I deleted and reposted because I don't see how to edit text. I forgot an essential "not" in one sentence, see below: 

Hi Pat, 

Thanks for the quick reply. 

I see what you are saying, but I have seen ways to calculate p-values for bootstrapped samples (i.e., empirical calculations of p from bootstrap samples). See (http://support.sas.com/resources/papers/proceedings10/329-2010.pdf) pages 11-14 for an example of doing this, or (https://blogs.sas.com/content/iml/2011/11/02/how-to-compute-p-values-for-a-bootstrap-distribution.html) for a simplified explanation by the same author. 

The p-value reported when requesting boot.ci.type = "bca.simple" is outputting significance test using the normal distribution (which should happen when you call boot.ci.type = "norm"), and therefore mismatches confidence intervals  in "bca.simple" which are not related to a normal distribution. This seems like a bug to me, even knowing what you said... 

But if we have built these confidence intervals, shouldn't this p-value either not be outputted and we just see if the CI overlaps with 0 (to prevent mis-interpretation) or give an empirical calculation of p? 

I ask because this is to be submitted to a journal for publication which requires exact p-values, and I am unsure how to proceed.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: (Possible) Bug with outputting p-values/CIs for lavaan(..., se = boot)
parts: I have seen ways to calculate p-values for bootstrapped samples (i.e., empirical calculations of p from bootstrap samples).

That is not what lavaan does.  It calculates normal-theory SEs, z stats, and p values in parameterEstimates(), which is called by summary().  Only the CIs are percentile (or bias-corrected, if requested).

This seems like a bug to me ... if we have built these confidence intervals, shouldn't this p-value either not be outputted and we just see if the CI overlaps with 0 (to prevent mis-interpretation) or give an empirical calculation of p? 

It is not a bug (which would be a mistake in the source code), but it is a sensible "feature request" you could post as an issue on GitHub:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
